stem.text: An air bubble in a tank of water is rising with terminal (constant) velocity. The forces acting on the bubble are $X$, $Y$ and $Z$, as shown.

stem.alt: Diagram of a vertical line with an arrow labelled X pointing up and arrows labelled Y and Z pointing down, meeting a small circle labelled air bubble, with an arrow labelled velocity pointing up beside it.

stem.text: The upthrust on the bubble is $X$.
Which statement about the forces is correct?

A.text: $Z$ is the viscous force on the bubble, $Y$ is the weight of the bubble and $X = Y + Z$.

B.text: $Z$ is the viscous force on the bubble, $Y$ is the weight of the bubble and $X > Y + Z$.

C.text: $Z$ is the weight of the bubble, $Y$ is the viscous force on the bubble and $X = Y + Z$.

D.text: $Z$ is the weight of the bubble, $Y$ is the viscous force on the bubble and $X > Y + Z$.
